note: Personal annual “decision review” given to the agent: the user's calendar + notes + spending records + travel records + personal journal + task list from the past year. The user says: “Help me review the important decisions I made over the past year; which decisions actually failed to meet expectations? If I could do it again, what would you advise me to do?” The agent needs to: first identify “important decisions” from fragmented information, for example changing gyms, buying equipment, taking courses, traveling, moving, subscribing to services, adjusting work arrangements, etc.; then find the background of when the decision was made, the goal at the time, and what actually happened afterwards; finally compare expected outcome vs actual outcome and find the recurring decision patterns. Difficulty: the data does not directly say “this is a decision”, so the agent must discover it itself; at the same time, it cannot simply judge failure based on spending — it needs to reconstruct the goal at the time. Tests longitudinal reasoning + causal/counterfactual reasoning + personal memory
env_description: life_review/: journal/ (4 months of diaries recording the goal at the time of each decision), notes.md (random thoughts), spending.csv (quantifiable actual usage: fitness 12 times / English 15 times / drone lens unopened), travel_records.csv, calendar.ics (cross-validate attendance against the spending records), todo_list.md (comparison of New Year resolutions with actuals); decisions must be identified by the agent itself, and expected vs actual requires cross-file reasoning
